newsitem.title: USA: Mazda kills off MX-6 coupe because of slow sales.
newsitem.headline: Mazda kills off MX-6 coupe because of slow sales.

text.p: Mazda Motor of America Inc., the U.S. arm of Mazda Motor Corp., said Friday it will discontinue its slow-selling Mazda MX-6 sport coupe when current inventories are exhausted by the end of 1997.
The MX-6 is the Mazda version of the Ford Probe, which Ford Motor Co. said Monday it will discontinue as part of a restructuring of its North American vehicle lineup.

"We have chosen to focus our available resources on supporting our core vehicle lines -- Protege, 626, MPV and B-Series truck," said George McCabe, senior vice president and general manager for Mazda Motor of America, in a statement.
The Mazda MX-6 was first introduced as a 1988 model. A second-generation MX-6 was introduced in 1993. Sales peaked in 1989 at 41,532 units and totaled 6,550 units in 1996.
Production will continue at Auto Alliance International in Flat Rock, Mich., through the end of the scheduled production year, ending May 30. Auto Alliance is a joint venture of Mazda and Ford.

Mazda said the plant will continue to make the 626 sedan. Mazda spokesman Fred Aikins said the company does not expect the decision to significantly affect the plant work force because production of the MX-6 was so limited.
"At this point, it looks like there will be no long-term effect," he said.
McCabe said the MX-6 is a victim of the market preference for sedans and light trucks instead of two-doors.
"While we are sorry to see the MX-6 go, in the long run this can only be viewed as a sound business decision for Mazda and our dealers," he said.
